Trump to kick off Asia trip with Quad talks in Manila
US President Donald Trump is flying to the Philippines at the tail end of a Southeast Asian summit, where he could face protests ahead of the first meeting in two years of the leaders of the Quad group of Indo-Pacific countries.
Trump's Asia trip, which also includes the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation forum in Shenzhen and a much-anticipated trilateral meeting with his Chinese and Russian counterparts, comes after his Republican Party's defeat in midterm elections and spy allegations that could complicate a fragile trade-war truce between the US and China.
There could be protests in Manila against Trump's visit, after days of demonstrations that have included the burning of effigies of the president and calls for an end to the Middle East war and the scrapping of the US-led Pax Silica initiative.
The meeting of the Quad ? the US, Australia, Japan and India ? will be Trump's first and takes place two years after the last gathering of the group, which his predecessor Joe Biden regarded as a signature foreign policy initiative.
It comes just ahead of the APEC gathering hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping, who has previously objected to the Quad as an effort to encircle Beijing. Quad members have said the grouping is not directed against any one country.
At the ASEAN summit on Monday, Chinese Premier Li Qiang hailed what he called "truly extraordinary" economic achievements of China and ASEAN in the face of global trade restrictions, expressing Beijing's commitment to free trade and the need to "stand united, ward off interference, and work together".
China is ASEAN's biggest trading partner and a key source of investment, but the biggest economies of the 11-member bloc ? which has a combined GDP of more than $US3.9 trillion ($A5.8 trillion) ? want to deepen ties with the United States despite protracted trade and diplomatic uncertainty under the Trump administration.
Former US Deputy Secretary of State Kurt Campbell credited Washington's top diplomat, Marco Rubio, with the timing and reconvening of the Quad, which he said had lost ambition under Trump.
"Part of what he (Rubio) is thinking is that this is probably the best possible signal if you're going to go into a trilateral meeting," said Campbell, co-founder of The Asia Group, referring to Thursday's US-China-Russia talks.
Before Trump's late afternoon arrival, ASEAN will hold meetings on Tuesday with leaders of Japan, South Korea, China and India, ahead of the annual East Asia Summit.

Trump Says He 'May Meet With Kim Jong Un' During Asia Trip — as Prez Declares It's 'Up to President Xi'
Nov. 16 2026, Published 3:20 p.m. ET
President Donald Trump said he may meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China during his Asia trip, RadarOnline.com has learned.
Trump is also preparing for unprecedented three-way nuclear discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Possible Kim Jong Un Meeting?
Speaking to reporters outside the White House on Monday, November 16, before departing, Trump said, “And we may meet with Kim Jong Un also. So, that'll be good… We might have Kim Jong Un. He may come, I don't know. That's up to President Xi."
Asked where any meeting would occur, he answered, "In China." According to a report, the president specifically suggested Shenzhen.
Trump previously met Kim three times during his first term: in Singapore in 2018, Hanoi in 2019, and at the Korean Demilitarized Zone later that year.
However, Trump has not secured meaningful engagement since returning to office. In August, he ordered the Pentagon to scale back joint military exercises with South Korea.
Three-Way Nuclear Talks
Trump is expected to take part in the first-ever three-way discussions with Xi and Putin focused on nuclear stockpiles and disarmament.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning called the talks of "groundbreaking significance," saying, "Under the current circumstances, the three countries shoulder an important responsibility to work together in addressing global challenges."
Trump identified denuclearization as a primary topic: "So we’re going to talk about denuclearization. Tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes, right?"
Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov said a separate bilateral Trump-Putin meeting was also being arranged: "I can say with 100 percent certainty that since both Putin and Donald Trump will be in Shenzhen, they will undoubtedly meet."
Ukraine, Iran and Broader Agenda
Despite earlier indications from administration officials that Ukraine would be sidelined, Trump said he intends to raise the war: "We'll talk about my favorite subject, Ukraine. Ukraine's losing Ukraine. Russia is losing 25,000 soldiers in the month."
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has warned against a "Yalta 2" redistribution of influence. The ongoing Iran conflict is also expected to feature.
Trump's itinerary includes the ASEAN summit in Manila, where he plans a trade agreement with Thailand, followed by the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
Economic issues, technology supply chains, and regional security will be central.
Elon Musk is Joining Trump; Nvidia Drama Continues
The trip comes after Republican midterm losses and a recent nationwide air-travel disruption.
Elon Musk is among those accompanying the president.
Controversy surrounding Nvidia and its former CEO Jensen Huang is expected to linger during the China visit, though U.S. officials said Trump did not plan to raise it with Xi.

Trump heads to Asia for historic nuclear talks with Xi, Putin, may meet Kim Jong Un
Donald Trump will visit Asia for trade negotiations and talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. The tour could revive North Korea diplomacy and open unprecedented trilateral nuclear discussions.
US President Donald Trump is heading to Asia on Monday for a high-stakes diplomatic tour centred on economic deals, renewed engagement with North Korea and unprecedented three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump said he may also meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his visit to China, as Washington looks to revive diplomatic engagement with Pyongyang over its nuclear programme.
Before departing the White House, Trump said discussions with Xi and Putin would also cover Russia's ongoing war with Ukraine, despite administration officials previously indicating that the conflict would not be on the agenda.
"We'll talk about my favourite subject, Ukraine. Ukraine's losing Ukraine," Trump told reporters. He also claimed Russia was losing 25,000 soldiers every month in the conflict.
Trump's Asia trip comes at a politically challenging time for his administration, following the Republican Party's losses in both chambers of Congress in the November midterm elections and mounting criticism over nationwide flight disruptions.
The visit also gives Trump an opportunity to shift attention towards foreign policy and trade negotiations as his administration navigates a changed political landscape in Washington.
NVIDIA CONTROVERSY CASTS SHADOW OVER CHINA VISIT
The controversy surrounding chipmaker Nvidia and its former CEO Jensen Huang is also expected to remain in the background during Trump's China visit.
Huang resigned as CEO last week after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese government agent. Beijing has denied involvement in the matter.
US officials said Trump had no plans to raise the controversy with Xi during their meeting.
The issue has attracted scrutiny over the Commerce Department's delay in imposing restrictions on Nvidia chip exports to a company led by the alleged Chinese agent.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, speaking to Fox News Channel anchor Larry Kudlow on Sunday, said the focus should be on whether Nvidia had maintained a culture of compliance with US export restrictions.
"Jensen Huang is an incredible innovator, but that does not abrogate their duties of compliance," Bessent said, adding that answers on the matter would emerge.
Huang had accompanied Trump aboard Air Force One during his previous visit to China in May and had maintained frequent contact with the president.
TRUMP HOPES TO REVIVE TALKS WITH KIM JONG
Trump also indicated that he could meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his China visit. The two leaders held three meetings during Trump's first term, but diplomatic engagement has remained limited since he returned to the White House.
The US president has been seeking to lay the groundwork for renewed talks on North Korea's nuclear programme. In August, he ordered the Pentagon to scale back joint military exercises with South Korea.
TRADE DEALS AND NUCLEAR DISARMAMENT ON AGENDA
Trump's trip will begin in Manila, where he is scheduled to meet Southeast Asian leaders concerned about China's growing influence and assertiveness in the region.
The White House said Trump would sign a trade deal with Thailand during his Philippines visit before travelling to China's technology hub of Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.
The highlight of the visit will be the first-ever trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin, focusing on nuclear stockpiles and disarmament.
The discussions will also take place against the backdrop of the ongoing US war with Iran, which has been widely blamed for the Republican Party's losses in the midterm elections. Iran has maintained close ties with both China and Russia.
Trump has sought to downplay the possibility of resuming major military strikes against Iran while also expressing little interest in further negotiations.
China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning described the proposed trilateral talks as having "groundbreaking significance".
She said the three countries had an important responsibility to work together to address global challenges and that Beijing aimed to hold in-depth discussions on safeguarding world peace and promoting stability.

sources.news_title: POLITICS: Trump Says Kim Jong Un’s Appearance at Shenzhen Summit Is Up to Xi – The Beltway Report
sources.text:
🔴 Website 👉 https://u-s-news.com/
Telegram 👉 https://t.me/usnewscom_channel
President Donald Trump said Monday that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could potentially appear during his upcoming trip to China, though he stressed the decision would rest with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
“We might have Kim Jong Un. He may come, I don’t know. That’s up to President Xi,” Trump told reporters during a White House gaggle.
The remark came when a reporter asked whether North Korea’s nuclear program would come up during Trump’s planned meetings with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen.
Trump and Kim last met in person in 2019 at a summit in Hanoi that ended without a deal on North Korea’s nuclear weapons program. Since then, Pyongyang has continued expanding its nuclear and missile capabilities, and talks between the two sides have remained stalled. Trump said in August he expected to meet Kim “later this year,” but North Korea pushed back on that timeline. Kim Yo Jong said the relationship between the two leaders remained “excellent” while accusing Washington of maintaining hostile policies toward Pyongyang, according to a Fox News Digital report at the time.
A U.S. official told ABC News last week that there were no plans for North Korea engagement during Trump’s Asia trip, and analysts say the topic is unlikely to be a major focus of the trilateral talks.
South Korea Pushes for a Seat at the Table
South Korea’s Foreign Ministry said it hoped high-level talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit would contribute to peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula, according to South Korean news outlet Yonhap News Agency. South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun reportedly raised the possibility of renewed U.S.-North Korea dialogue during a meeting with his Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, in Beijing on Friday, stressing that Seoul has vital interests in Korean Peninsula issues and wants its perspective considered.
Andrew Yeo, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told Yonhap that North Korea’s nuclear program is unlikely to come up at the summit given differences between Washington and Moscow over Pyongyang’s nuclear ambitions. Ellen Kim, a senior fellow at the Korea Economic Institute, suggested the leaders might briefly touch on North Korea in private, but said nuclear arms control and the war in Iran are likely to take priority. She added that Xi or Putin could potentially relay a message from Trump to Kim, though both leaders may be reluctant to support direct U.S.-North Korea talks for fear of losing their own leverage over Pyongyang.
A Packed Agenda in Shenzhen
The trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin is scheduled for 2:30 p.m. Thursday local time at Shenzhen Kylin Villa, according to Trump’s public schedule. White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said Friday that Trump plans to discuss nuclear arms reduction with Xi and Putin, while a senior U.S. official said Iran would also be on the agenda. The Associated Press reported Monday that Trump intends to raise Russia’s war in Ukraine during the talks as well.
Asked Monday what it would take for Putin to back down from the war in Ukraine, Trump offered a mixed assessment of the Russian leader’s posture.
“I think he’s backing down a little bit. I think he could be tougher. I think it could be a lot tougher, frankly,” Trump told reporters outside the White House.
Fox News Digital reported it had reached out to the White House for additional comment.

sources.news_title: Trump Departs for Asia, Says He May Meet with Kim Jong-un
sources.text:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump told reporters Monday, as he departed for Asia, that North Korean dictator Kim Jong-un may join his trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump jetted off to the Philippines, where he will attend an Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit Tuesday before attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leadership meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday.
The president spoke with reporters on the South Lawn of the White House before his departure and said he plans to meet with Xi and Putin while in China, and that he could also meet with Kim.
“We’re going to the Philippines, big meeting… mostly on economics, but a lot of other things will be discussed, and economically, we’re leading every country in the world by a lot… I’m making a major speech,” Trump said.
“And then we go to China, and we’ll be with President Xi. He was here a month ago, and we’re also going to meet with President Putin, and we may meet with Kim Jong-Un also, so that’ll be good,” he added. “We have a chance to accomplish a lot.”
WATCH:
Trump met with Kim on three occasions during his first term. They met in Singapore in 2018, then in Hanoi, Vietnam, and in the Korean Demilitarized Zone in 2019. Trump became the first U.S. president to visit North Korea, and the series of meetings marked progress toward civil relations between the U.S. and the communist state.
Progress stalled when former President Joe Biden entered office, as that administration largely ignored the region for four years. Kim, however, continued to demonstrate warmth toward Trump during his hiatus from office, sending Trump and his family a letter of sympathy after his near-assassination in July 2024.
Trump said it is up to Xi whether or not Kim will attend the meeting.
Topics for the trilateral meeting will include denuclearization, Iran, Ukraine, economics, and trade, according to the president.
“We’re going to talk about denuclearization; tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes, right?” he said.
“We’ll talk about Iran. We have Iran in very good shape… We’ll talk about my favorite subject: Ukraine… Ukraine-Russia is losing 25,000 soldiers a month. We’ll be talking about that. We’ll all be talking about economics and trade,” Trump added.

sources.news_title: Trump to Meet With Putin and Xi at First-Ever Trilateral Summit in China–May Also Meet With Kim Jong Un › American Greatness
sources.text:
President Donald Trump departed the White House Monday, to begin a multi-day trip to Asia that includes the first-ever trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump said this morning that he may also meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his visit to China later this week.
“We’ll be with President Xi. He was here a month ago, and we’re also going to meet with President Putin, and we may meet with Kim Jong Un also. So that’ll be good. We have a chance to accomplish a lot,” Trump told reporters as he left the White House.
The president is traveling this week to Manila, Philippines and Shenzhen, China, for a pair of summits to discuss nuclear disarmament issues and the war with Iran.
On the first leg of the trip, Trump will meet with the “Quad” allies (Japan, India, Australia) in the Philippines, where he is expected to sign a trade deal with Thailand and address Southeast Asian concerns regarding China’s regional aggression.
The summit in Shenzhen later in the week will reportedly focus on nuclear stockpile reduction, the war in Iran, and potentially Russia’s war in Ukraine, marking the first time the leaders of the U.S., China, and Russia have met together.
A senior White House official told reporters on Friday that there were “no plans at all for engagement with North Korea,” though Trump said back in August that he would try to meet with Kim Jong Un this year to reengage on nuclear issues.
The president met with Kim several times during his first term in office, including in 2019 when Trump became the first sitting U.S. president to step inside North Korea at the Korean Demilitarized Zone.
The U.S. delegation on Air Force One includes Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett, and Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino.
Trillionaire Elon Musk will join the delegation for the China leg of the trip, traveling as an advisor given his business interests in the U.S.–China relationship. He will not participate in the trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin or the bilateral Trump–Xi session, officials said.
Notably absent is former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who accompanied Trump to China in May but resigned last week amid the alleged Chinese-spy affair scandal.

sources.news_title: Trump outlines Asia trip, calls for FAA upgrades, raises possibility of meeting Kim Jong Un
sources.text:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump fielded questions from reporters Monday morning on the White House South Lawn as he departed for an Asia trip focused on economic meetings and talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. He raised the possibility of also meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and addressed the recent FAA ground stop, Nvidia leadership, immigration and other issues.
Trump said the trip would begin with meetings in the Philippines centered mostly on economics.
“We’re going to the Philippines, a big meeting on mostly on economics, but a lot of other things will be discussed,” he said. “Then we go to China, and we’ll be with President Xi. He was here a month ago, and we’re also going to meet with President Putin, and we may meet with Kim Jong Un also. So that’ll be good. We have a chance to accomplish a lot.”
He later added that any meeting with Kim would be up to Xi. Trump has previously met Kim three times during his first term.
FAA air traffic upgrades and Friday outage
Trump called for billions in congressional funding to replace aging air traffic control equipment after Friday’s nationwide ground stop.
“We essentially want to blow it up and put new in, and we can do it simultaneously with very little trouble,” he said. “So that’s what we’re doing. But we need the funding to get it done. But essentially, what you saw on Friday was very, very old equipment that had a heart attack.”
He described some equipment as more than 50 years old and said the administration has sought funding for two years.
“We’ve been trying to get the money for two years to fix it, and Buttigieg ruined the system. He totally ruined it,” Trump said, referring to former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg. “The Democrats […] really set back the system a long way.”
Responding to questions about his involvement during the outage, Trump said he was at the White House.
“I was in the Oval Office,” he said, adding that he held meetings with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and others. He said the system was restored within hours.
Nvidia leadership and Jensen Huang
Trump said he would not mind seeing former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang return to the company after Huang’s resignation amid an admitted affair and questions about whether the woman involved is a Chinese spy.
“I would not mind. I would not mind that,” Trump said. “I would say that Jensen’s reinstatement, I think he learned a big lesson, I guess maybe one lesson more important than another. But I would certainly not mind seeing that.”

Trump may meet Kim Jong Un in China during East Asia trip, hints at talks with North Korean leader
Donald Trump says he may meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China during his East Asia trip, raising the possibility of fresh US-North Korea talks.
US President Donald Trump said on Monday he might meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China this week, an announcement that could dramatically reshape his trip through East Asia.
The president met the North Korean leader several times during his 2017-2021 first term in unprecedented direct diplomacy that failed to persuade Kim to give up his nuclear weapons.
Trump has repeatedly expressed interest in another meeting during his current term, but also previously previewed meetings with Kim that never took place, including during a trip to Asia last year.
Senior US officials have previously said he has no immediate plans for another meeting, while North Korea has said it sees no need for talks at this time and denounced hostile US policies.
Trump told reporters while departing the White House en route to the Philippines and China that any meeting would occur in China, and that the North Korean leader's presence was ultimately up to Chinese President Xi Jinping.
"(Xi) was here ... and we're also going to meet with (Russian) President Putin, and we may meet with Kim Jong Un also," Trump said.
"So that'll be good. We have a chance to accomplish a lot."
Also read: Trump held up to $62 million in Nvidia stock by August 2026, report says
Deep Dive
Trump added in reference to Kim: "He may come. I don't know. That's up to President Xi."
North Korea's mission to the United Nations did not respond to a request for comment on Trump's remarks.
The Kremlin said on Monday a planned meeting between Putin, Trump and Xi on the sidelines of this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in China would have a major impact on global affairs.
Trump said he would discuss denuclearization, Iran and Ukraine with Xi and Putin, as well as trade and the economy, but US officials and analysts have played down the possibility of a meaningful agreement emerging.
Russia's Interfax news agency quoted Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov as saying later on Monday that Putin could meet Kim if he comes to China.
North Korea has sent about 14,000 to 15,000 troops to support Russia's war in Ukraine since 2024, according to Ukrainian and South Korean estimates, with most deployed in the Kursk region to help repel a Ukrainian incursion.
Victor Cha, head of the Korea program at Washington's Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank, said Trump's comments made clear he had asked Xi to bring Kim to China for a meeting.
"One could see a huge diplomatic victory for Kim if he were to share a stage with the US, Russia, China ... the three other nuclear powers in Asia - in addition to any bilateral with Trump," he said.
"The common narrative is that China would not want to distract from their hosting APEC but I think Xi’s global diplomacy offensive would probably be enhanced, in his mind, if he were bringing together all of the leaders for this extraordinary meeting," Cha said.
Trump's interest in renewed engagement with Kim comes seven years after their last summit ended without agreement when they failed to bridge differences over North Korea's nuclear weapons and sanctions relief.
Since then, North Korea has significantly expanded its nuclear and missile capabilities while strengthening ties with Russia and China, and any willingness by Trump to make major concessions to Pyongyang risks creating friction with regional allies.
Trump has referred to North Korea as a nuclear power, a status allies in the region and the West have refused to recognize despite the dozens of nuclear warheads experts believe Pyongyang has built.

sources.text:
President Donald Trump has teased a possible first meeting in seven years with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, at the APEC summit in China.
Headlines ahead of this week's summit in Shenzen have focused on Trump meeting his Chinese and Russian counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, in the hope for a breakthrough on the Ukraine War.
But Trump said that a meeting with the North Korean leader was also on the cards, as the U.S. seeks to reengage with Pyongyang over its nuclear capabilities.
Read More on World
"The likelihood of Kim Jong Un meeting Trump has risen, even if only slightly, especially since the midterm elections results," Edward Howell, author of A New Axis of Upheaval: North Korea, Russia, China, Iran, told Newsweek on Monday.
"With Trump in a weakened position, Pyongyang might choose to respond to any U.S. calls for engagement, on the proviso that North Korea does not offer any nuclear concessions, let alone substantive nuclear concessions in any talks," he added.
When contacted for further information, the White House referred Newsweek to the president's statements.
Newsweek has also reached out to the North Korean embassy in London for further comment.
What Did Trump Say About APEC Trip?
Trump's Kim revelation came as he told reporters about his trip to the annual summit of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) bloc of 21 members.
He said his schedule includes meetings with Association of Southeast Asian Nations leaders in Manila, the Philippines where there will be "big meetings, mostly on economics."
"Then we'll go to China and we'll be with President Xi, he was here a month ago," said Trump, referring to state visit to Washington, "and we are also going to meet with President Putin."
The meeting with the Russian and Chinese leaders will be the first among the three leaders which the White House said would aim at decreasing the proliferation of nuclear weapons as the war in Ukraine continues to rage.
The trio are also likely to discuss Iran.
Trump's announcement about the North Korean leader came as a surprise. "We may meet with Kim Jong Un also. So that'll be good. We have a chance to accomplish a lot," Trump added.
Howell, who is a lecturer and research fellow at the University of Oxford, England said that any Trump-Kim meeting would fulfill Trump’s desire for interpersonal dialogue with the North Korean leader.
For North Korea, too, Pyongyang would continue to receive material and humanitarian assistance from Russia, all the while framing any meeting with the U.S. as recognition of North Korea as a nuclear weapons state, he added.
"That said, Kim Jong Un has repeatedly asserted that any dialogue must be premised on the U.S. making clear that North Korea is a nuclear weapons state, a precondition which Washington, of course, is unwilling to take."
The U.S. president is also scheduled to meet with leaders from Quad, a group consisting of the United States, India, Australia and Japan.
Trump is also scheduled to sign a trade deal with Thailand and attend a dinner with leaders of the Southeast Asian Nations and other regional leaders.
When Have Trump And Kim Met Before?
Trump and Kim have met three times, all during the president's first term.
The first ever summit between a sitting U.S. president and a North Korean leader took place on June 12, 2018, in Singapore.
They issued a joint statement on U.S.-North Korean security guarantees and a commitment by Pyongyang to work toward denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula.
The next meeting took place in Hanoi, Vietnam on February 27 in which the pair discussed North Korea’s nuclear and missile programs, as well as the establishment of a new relationship between the two countries.
The pair's third and most recent face-to-face meeting took place on June 30, 2019 when Trump crossed the demarcation line of the DMZ and became the first sitting U.S. president to enter North Korea.
"Whether or not Trump and Kim meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit—as was also speculated last year—remains to be seen," said Howell.

sources.text:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he may meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during an upcoming visit to China, where he also expects to hold talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The White House previously confirmed the trilateral summit, with Iran and nuclear arms control among the planned topics.
"We might have Kim Jong Un; he may come. I don't know. That's up to President Xi," Trump told reporters when asked whether North Korea's denuclearization would be discussed during the meetings.
Trump said Iran would also be on the agenda during his talks with the Russian and Chinese leaders. His remarks came as the US expanded its military presence in the Middle East, bringing the number of American aircraft carrier strike groups in the region to three.
"We'll talk about Iran. We have Iran in very good shape, but we'll talk about Iran a little bit," he said.
The president outlined a busy diplomatic schedule, beginning with a visit to the Philippines that he said would focus primarily on economic issues. Trump claimed that the United States is "leading every country in the world by a lot" and said Philippine officials had asked him to deliver a major speech.
Senior officials accompanying Trump
The White House released a list of 15 senior officials who will accompany Trump on his diplomatic trip, with the delegation including Secretary of State Marco Rubio, newly appointed White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, and US Trade Representative Ambassador Jamieson Greer.
Miller, who assumed his new position last week following the departure of Susie Wiles, will travel alongside other senior officials from the president's inner circle.
Among those accompanying Trump are deputy chief of staff Dan Scavino, one of the president's longtime confidants; deputy chief of staff for operations Beau Harrison; White House communications director Steven Cheung; and National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett.
The delegation will also include staff members who work closely with the president, including his personal assistant Natalie Harp and social media director Margo Martin.
Ambassador Monica Crowley, who oversees protocol at the US State Department, will also participate in the trip.
Trump outlines China summit and nuclear talks
Following the stop in the Philippines, Trump will travel to China for talks with Xi, who visited Washington a month earlier. Trump said he also expects to meet Putin and suggested Kim could join the discussions.
Trump also described denuclearization as a "tough subject," arguing that countries are reluctant to give up their nuclear weapons while other nations retain theirs.
Turning to the war in Ukraine, which he called his "favorite subject," Trump claimed that Ukraine is losing the conflict and that Russia is losing 25,000 soldiers each month.
He said he believes Putin is "backing down a little bit" but warned that the Russian president "could be a lot tougher."
Trump also pointed to the December G20 summit in Miami as another important diplomatic event, describing his upcoming engagements as "a chance to accomplish a lot."
Asked whether Republican losses in the midterm elections could weaken his influence abroad, Trump dismissed the suggestion. He noted that similar or worse election results had occurred previously and emphasized that his name had not been on the ballot.
He attributed some of the dissatisfaction among Republican voters to legislation passed by Congress, saying those concerns would need to be addressed.
On immigration, Trump said he would consider reforms if asked, but insisted that any changes must be strict and exclude amnesty.
He also warned that migrant caravans approaching the US border "will not be allowed in," threatening heavy tariffs against Mexico if its government failed to stop them.
Asked whether he would pressure China to stop purchasing Iranian oil, Trump declined to disclose his negotiating plans, saying he would raise whatever issues he considered necessary without informing reporters in advance.
Trump addresses Nvidia controversy and China chip sales
Trump also faced questions about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned following allegations of an affair with a Chinese woman identified in intelligence reporting as a possible spy.
The president cautioned against treating the allegation as established fact, saying he did not know whether the woman was a spy and that "nobody's proven that."
Trump suggested that attractive women from China are frequently suspected of espionage and said he had not heard the allegation from Rubio.
Turning to US semiconductor export restrictions, Trump said Huang "wanted to sell to China" but had been permitted to export only "chips that were sort of obsolete."
He compared the restrictions to limitations on selling older aviation equipment, noting that Nvidia had been prohibited from exporting its Blackwell chips and other advanced technology.
Trump argued that even Blackwell chips, Nvidia's latest generation of AI chips, would become outdated within two years and defended the sale of less advanced products as "a good thing, not a bad thing."
Asked whether his relationship with Huang had created national security risks, Trump insisted that security "was not put at risk."
He maintained that the United States is "now stronger than ever before," both militarily and economically, pointing to increased production of Patriot missile systems and other defense equipment, as well as the opening of new military manufacturing facilities across the country.
Trump also suggested that Huang could return to his former position, saying "Jensen's reinstatement" would not concern him because Huang had "learned a big lesson."
He added that "a lot of people are asking" for Huang's return and that "that certainly isn't a bad idea."
Trump said he had also recommended former Apple CEO Tim Cook for a role, without providing further details.
While acknowledging that the personal conduct at the center of the controversy was something "we probably shouldn't have been doing," he distinguished it from the unproven espionage allegation.
Trump blames aging aviation systems for Friday disruption
Trump also addressed a major aviation systems failure on Friday, blaming decades of inadequate investment in US air traffic control infrastructure. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy had previously attributed the nationwide ground stop to aging equipment that became overloaded with data.
The president repeatedly described the equipment involved as "very, very old," saying some components were more than 50 years old.
He said the system "had a heart attack" and argued that the government must replace aging equipment with modern technology.
Trump described the objective as to "blow it up and put new in," while operating the existing and replacement systems simultaneously to minimize disruptions.
He said the transition could be completed with "very little trouble," provided Congress approves the necessary funding.
The president accused the previous administration of making costly technical mistakes, particularly by connecting copper wiring to glass-based systems. He argued that the approach was incompatible with electrical engineering principles and had wasted public money.
Trump praised Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and other officials for their handling of Friday's disruption, emphasizing that "everybody was safe" and that there were "no crashes."
He rejected personal responsibility for the incident, attributing the failure to decades of neglect involving equipment that was "probably on average 50 years old."
Asked why he had focused on renovating the White House while aviation infrastructure remained in poor condition, Trump defended the construction work at the executive mansion.
He said the building had suffered from 18 broken windows, deteriorating exterior plaster and damaged columns concealed beneath "100 coats of paint."
Trump maintained he spent only "10 minutes a day" overseeing the repairs and personally covered their cost.
He claimed the White House was now "better than it was in 1792," called the expense "peanuts," and said visiting foreign leaders had noticed the improvements.
Despite his criticism of the aging aviation infrastructure, Trump insisted that commercial flights remain "very safe."
However, he said the US should have "the best system in the world" and urged Congress to approve funding his administration has sought for two years.
Trump also criticized former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, accusing him of having "totally ruined" the system. He argued that Democratic policies had "really set back" efforts to modernize the nation's aviation infrastructure.
The US president expressed confidence that Friday's incident would persuade lawmakers to provide the funding needed to overhaul the system.

Trump’s departure comes after the often-omnipresent president had remained largely out of public sight for the past several days, even as a nationwide ground stop snarled air traffic and his Republican administration faced tough questions on its handling of the situation.
His trip to Asia, which begins in Manila then continues to the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen, gives Trump the opportunity to change the narrative from his domestic woes, including the air travel problems and fallout from the November midterm election where his party lost both chambers of Congress.
